identity.purpose: Names, versions, counts, timestamps — anything that is data, set tabular.

subject.purpose: A Resource Detail page's own name — the one piece of text set larger and bolder than everything around it.

motion.name: flip-reveal
motion.purpose: The departure board's one signature move. Plays on first paint (staggered per roster row, 40ms apart, capped 400ms) and whenever a watched value changes. Disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Status Dot
components.description: A filled circle in one of the three reserved health colors. The system's only recurring iconography.
components.css: .ds-status-dot { display: inline-block; width: 0.5rem; height: 0.5rem; border-radius: 9999px; background-color: #10b981; }

components.name: Flip Value
components.description: Wraps any value that should play the flip-reveal signature motion on first paint or on change.
components.css: .ds-flip-value { display: inline-block; transform-origin: 50% 0%; animation: ds-flip-reveal 420ms cubic-bezier(0.16,0,0.3,1) both; } @keyframes ds-flip-reveal { 0% { transform: rotateX(90deg); opacity: 0.4; } 60% { transform: rotateX(-12deg); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: rotateX(0deg); opacity: 1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flip-value { animation: none; } }

components.name: Resource Table
components.description: The shared table shell for every tabular list — hairline rows, sticky header within a scroll ancestor, dropped last-column gap.
components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; text-align: left; } .ds-table thead tr { position: sticky; top: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #1f252b; background: #0b0e11; font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #8b97a1; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { padding: 0.5rem 1.5rem 0.5rem 0; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-table th:last-child, .ds-table td:last-child { padding-right: 0; } .ds-table tbody tr { border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(31,37,43,0.6); }

components.name: Detail Header
components.description: A Resource Detail page's header: an optional health dot, a muted kind/namespace prefix, and the Resource's own name set at full weight.
components.css: .ds-detail-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.025em; color: #e5e7eb; } .ds-detail-prefix { color: #8b97a1; }

components.name: Collapsible Manifest
components.description: The one deliberate exception to curated data — a Resource's raw YAML, collapsed by default.
components.html:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
components.css: .ds-manifest-trigger { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #8b97a1; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-manifest-trigger:hover { color: #e5e7eb; } .ds-manifest-body { max-height: 24rem; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid #1f252b; background: #151a1e; border-radius: 0.375rem; padding: 0.75rem; font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #8b97a1; }

narrative.overview: Klyro's confirmed direction refuses the category default a Kubernetes dashboard always ships: a sidebar of KPI cards over a passive data table. Instead, every connected Cluster is a row on a live departure board, scanned top to bottom in under a second, with state changes that visibly flip into place rather than silently updating. The same restraint that makes a real departure board trustworthy — exactly the colors that carry meaning, nothing decorative — is Klyro's whole color discipline: three reserved health colors and nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black slate ground, never pure black
Tabular-figure monospace for every identity/numeric field; Inter for labels and prose
Hairline row dividers do the structural work a card grid would otherwise need
Exactly three reserved colors for health state, never used decoratively
One signature motion (the flip), triggered only by real state change or first paint

rules.name: The Three-Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red exist for exactly one job — Resource health — at every scale from a single Pod's own Ready condition up to a Cluster's aggregate. They never appear as a brand accent, a decorative highlight, or a fourth meaning.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any field that is a count, a version, a timestamp, or an identity string sets in the monospace stack with tabular-nums. Prose and labels never do.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every surface is flat. A raised state (hover, selection) is a background-color shift, never a shadow.

dos: Do reserve green/amber/red for health state only, at any zoom level.
Do set every identity/numeric value in the monospace stack with tabular-nums.
Do play the flip motion only on real state change or first paint.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation.
Do keep tables and hairlines as the structural device; reach for ResourceTable before inventing a new list shell.
donts: Don't add a fourth decorative accent color.
Don't add card shadows, gradients, or rounded-everything.
Don't scatter the flip motion across unrelated hovers or page transitions.
Don't build a new table/list component when ResourceTable already does the job.
Don't let the command palette, or any future control, read as a costume of a terminal.
